fdm.name: FDM — fused filament
fdm.description: Molten plastic laid down line by line. The workhorse: tough enough for parts that get used, cheap enough for parts you need twenty of, and it prints the largest volumes we offer.
fdm.bestFor: Best for: functional parts, enclosures, jigs, large models

sla.name: Resin — SLA/MSLA
sla.description: A screen cures a whole layer of liquid resin at once. Surfaces come out glass-smooth and detail survives that FDM would simply lose. Slower and pricier per gram, worth every satang when it matters.
sla.bestFor: Best for: miniatures, jewellery masters, dental models, tiny mechanisms

pla.name: PLA
pla.description: The default. Rigid, dimensionally accurate, prints crisply and costs the least. Softens around 60°C, so keep it out of a parked car.

pla-silk.name: Silk PLA
pla-silk.description: PLA with a glossy, almost metallic sheen. Same strength, much better looking — made for display pieces and gifts.

petg.name: PETG
petg.description: Tougher than PLA and far less brittle. Shrugs off water, sunlight and a drop onto concrete. The go-to for parts that live outdoors.

abs.name: ABS
abs.description: Holds its shape to around 100°C and can be sanded, drilled and glued with solvent. Lego is made of it, which tells you most of what you need.

tpu.name: TPU
tpu.description: Genuinely flexible — bends, squashes and springs back. Phone bumpers, gaskets, feet, grips and anything that has to absorb a knock.

pa12-cf.name: Carbon Nylon
pa12-cf.description: Nylon filled with chopped carbon fibre. Stiff, light and dimensionally stable under load. Our engineering material for tooling and brackets.

resin-standard.name: Standard Resin
resin-standard.description: Glass-smooth surfaces and detail down to 0.025 mm layers. Brittle by comparison, so it is for looking at, not for load.

resin-tough.name: Tough Resin
resin-tough.description: Resin detail with enough impact resistance to be handled, snapped together and used. Closer to ABS in feel.

resin-clear.name: Clear Resin
resin-clear.description: Transparent out of the printer, properly see-through once polished. Light pipes, lenses, covers and display models.

ultra.name: Ultra fine
ultra.detail: 0.08 mm · as good as FDM gets

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.subtitle: If yours is not here, message us on LINE — we answer quickly.

formats.q: What file formats do you accept?
formats.a: For 3D: STL, OBJ, 3MF and PLY. STL is the safest bet and every CAD package exports it. For paper printing: PDF is ideal because fonts and layout are locked in, but we also take JPG, PNG, DOCX, PPTX, AI and PSD.

noModel.q: I do not have a 3D model. Can you make one?
noModel.a: Yes. Send photographs, a sketch with dimensions, or the broken original and we will quote the modelling separately. Simple parts are usually ฿800–2,500.

accuracy.q: How accurate are the printed parts?
accuracy.a: FDM holds about ±0.3 mm or 0.5% of the dimension, whichever is larger. Resin is closer to ±0.1 mm. If a specific dimension has to be exact, tell us which one and we will compensate for it in the slicer.

quoteAccuracy.q: Is the instant quote the final price?
quoteAccuracy.a: It is accurate for the vast majority of jobs. We still open every file by hand before confirming, because a quote cannot see a 0.3 mm wall that will snap or an overhang that needs a lot of support. If something changes we tell you before we print.

strength.a: PLA unless you have a reason not to — it is cheapest and prints best. PETG if it will live outside or get wet. ABS if it will get hot. TPU if it needs to flex. Carbon nylon if it has to carry load. Resin if detail matters more than strength.

colours.q: Can I get a specific colour?
colours.a: We stock the colours shown on each material. Anything outside that we can usually order in within a few days, or we can print in grey and paint to a colour you specify.

lead.a: Standard 3D printing is five business days, express is two, and rush is next day. Paper printing is ready the following day as standard, same-day within four hours, or while you wait for small jobs. Big batches take longer and the quote tells you when.

delivery.a: Pickup at the shop is free. Bangkok delivery is ฿60 and next day, upcountry is ฿100 and about three days, and same-day express courier is ฿180. Orders over ฿2,000 ship free.

payment.a: Bank transfer or PromptPay once the quote is confirmed, or cash and card at the counter. Production runs over ฿10,000 are half up front, half on collection.

ip.a: You do. We use your file to print your job and nothing else, we never share it, and we delete it ninety days after the order closes unless you ask us to keep it on file for repeats.

minimum.a: ฿150 for 3D printing and ฿20 for paper printing. Small parts are often better combined onto one plate — ask and we will nest them for you.

bulk.a: Yes, up to a few hundred parts. Past that, injection moulding usually beats us on price and we will say so. We can also print you a mould master.

copyBook.q: Can you copy a whole book?
copyBook.a: We can copy bound originals, and we charge a small handling fee for the extra care. We will not reproduce copyrighted work in full — bring something you have the right to copy.

scan.q: Can you scan documents to PDF?
scan.a: Yes, A4 at ฿3 a page and A3 at ฿5, scanned at 300–600 dpi and sent by email or LINE. Searchable OCR is available on request.

paperSizes.q: Do you print bigger than A3?
paperSizes.a: Not in house. A3 is our largest sheet. For posters and banners above that we work with a wide-format partner nearby and can arrange it for you.
